newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Anglo wins Angola concessions, seeks more.
newsitem.headline: Anglo wins Angola concessions, seeks more.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said it had been awarded two exploration concessions in Angola this week and was seeking to acquire more.

Its Angolan subsidiary Anmercosa Exploration was officially awarded two concessions in the south of the country on Wednesday. The company had first applied for the concessions, totalling 26,000 square kilometres, in 1991.
Anglo has a three-year lease on the concessions and has committed $1 million on exploration in the first year.
It is now waiting for work permits to be approved for six geologists who will begin doing preliminary exploration on the concessions.
"We are very interested in acquiring additional concessions in Angola," said Brian King, Anglo American's senior regional exploration manager for Angola.
He said Anglo American would be exploring mainly for nickel, copper, zinc and gold deposits in the concessions located near the country's southern border with Namibia.
King said Anmercosa was in advanced negotiations to form a joint venture with a Portuguese company which also aims to gain exploration concessions in Angola.
"We have worked with (them) before," King said.
"We are creating this joint venture with a view toward acquiring more concessions here."
King also said the company was attempting to form join ventures with a number of individuals and companies that already have concessions in the country.
"We want to join up with some of the existing concessionaires," said King. "It would go a long way toward cutting down on all the government bureaucracy."
Angola produces some $1 billion worth of diamonds each year and over $4 billion in oil, but reserves of base and precious metals and other minerals were unproven.
"Angola has a lot of geology that is very interesting and has a lot of potential," said King.
